pages.title: CDir, CDentry and MDSCacheObject: the dirfrag/dentry object model

features.name: Reference counting with named pin types
features.description: Every cache object keeps a total ref count plus a per-pin-type ref_map (MDS_REF_SET is always defined). get() calls first_get() on 0->1, put() asserts on underflow per pin type and calls last_put() on 1->0. Objects are never deleted while referenced; deletion points are CDir::remove_dentry, CInode::close_dirfrag, MDCache::remove_inode. Pin ids: generic 1000-1011 (replicated, dirty, lock, request, waiter, dirtyscattered, authpin, ptrwaiter, tempexporting, clientlease, discoverbase, scrubqueue), CDir 1-12, CDentry 1-4.
features.notes: Pin counts are visible in admin dumps (pins{name: count}). Negative pin ids are only a naming convention; get() never checks them.

features.name: Upward pinning: referenced objects pin their ancestors
features.description: CDentry::first_get pins the dentry in the LRU; CDir::first_get takes CInode::PIN_DIRFRAG; CInode::first_get takes CDentry::PIN_INODEPIN on its primary dentry; a non-empty CDir holds PIN_CHILD. Hence the cache is always a connected tree from base inodes and only leaf dentries with no references are expirable.
features.notes: Trimming is leaf-first; memory pressure cannot evict ancestors of any open/locked/waited object.

features.name: NOTIFYREF stray notification on put
features.description: Objects with STATE_NOTIFYREF get _put() called on every put. CDentry::STATE_STRAY uses it: when only the dirty pin and the inode pin remain, maybe_eval_stray() lets the stray manager purge an unlinked inode as soon as its last user drops it.
features.notes: Underpins POSIX unlink-while-open semantics: data is purged only after the last reference (open caps) goes away.

features.name: Authority resolution and dir_auth delegation
features.description: CDentry authority = its dir; CDir authority = dir_auth if subtree root else inode authority; CInode authority = inode_auth if set, else parent dir, else first projected parent, else UNDEF. dir_auth (-1,-2) normal, (m,-2) delegation, (m1,m2) ambiguous during migration, (me,me) on an auth frozen tree root. set_dir_auth maintains num_subtree_roots, swaps the directory-inode auth pin of frozen dirs and wakes WAIT_SINGLEAUTH when auth becomes unambiguous.
features.notes: dir_auth.first is sent to clients as DirStat.auth.

features.name: Replica map and nonces
features.description: The authority keeps replica_map rank->nonce (PIN_REPLICATED while non-empty); add_replica returns 1 for a new replica or increments the nonce on re-replication; replicas store replica_nonce. MCacheExpire carries the replica's nonce and the authority drops expires with a stale nonce. EXPORT_NONCE=1 after migration.
features.notes: MDS-to-MDS only; irrelevant to clients except via DirStat.dist.

features.name: Auth pins with one-level nested accounting
features.description: auth_pins counts users of an object as its authority. Pins on a dentry or on a dentry's primary inode increment the dirfrag's dir_auth_pins (one level only). CDir pins do not propagate upward; while a tree freeze is in progress all member dirfrags also add to a shared freeze_tree_state->auth_pins counter. link/unlink/steal_dentry transfer existing pins.
features.notes: Main takers: requests, fetch/fetch_keys, commit, the freezer, fragmentation (prepare_old_fragment, fragment_freeze_dirs, _fragment_logged), lock caches, predirty_journal_parents; also ScrubStack, StrayManager purge, Migrator export and RecoveryQueue.

features.name: can_auth_pin errors and drop-everything-and-retry
features.description: can_auth_pin returns ERR_NOT_AUTH, ERR_FRAGMENTING_DIR (freezing/frozen dir), ERR_EXPORTING_TREE (freezing/frozen tree) or ERR_EXPORTING_INODE. When any object of a request cannot be auth-pinned, acquire_locks drops all locks and local auth pins, waits WAIT_UNFREEZE and retries the whole request (or aborts if nonblocking). Lock-cache owners may force pins. auth_pin itself never checks.
features.notes: A request never waits for authpinnability (an unfreeze) while holding local auth pins, which lets freezes make progress; it does keep auth pins (and locks) while waiting for locks after pinning (src/mds/Locker.cc:566-655), and keeps remote auth pins (notify_freeze_waiter).

features.name: freeze_dir (fragmentation quiescence)
features.description: freeze_dir auth-pins the dir; freezes immediately if no other pin on the dir and dir_auth_pins==0, else STATE_FREEZINGDIR and invalidates lock caches pinning it. maybe_finish_freeze completes when auth_pins==1 and dir_auth_pins==0. _freeze_dir sets STATE_FROZENDIR, PIN_FROZEN and auth-pins the dirfrag's own directory inode (non subtree root), which blocks the enclosing dirfrag from freezing. unfreeze_dir cancels (WAIT_FROZEN gets -1) or unfreezes (WAIT_UNFREEZE).
features.notes: Needed because split/merge moves CDentry objects between CDir objects.

features.name: freeze_tree (migration quiescence)
features.description: freeze_tree walks all nested non-subtree-root dirfrags, attaches a shared freeze_tree_state and sums auth_pins+dir_auth_pins; completes when the shared counter drops to the freezer's own pin. _freeze_tree turns dirfrags opened after the freeze started into separate subtree bounds and makes the root a subtree root with dir_auth (me,me). unfreeze_tree collects WAIT_UNFREEZE from all members; cancellation completes WAIT_FROZEN with -1. adjust_freeze_after_rename removes dirs renamed out of the freezing tree.
features.notes: Static counters num_freezing_trees/num_frozen_trees give a fast path for the common no-freeze case.

features.name: Stale freeze cancellation
features.description: If a freezing export or fragment's cumulative auth-pin count has not changed for mds_freeze_tree_timeout (30 s) and there are remote waiters or the parent dir is freezing, the export/fragment is cancelled to break cross-rank or nested freeze deadlocks.

features.name: Frozen inode tracking and lock-cache suppression
features.description: Each dirfrag tracks freezing_inodes and num_frozen_inodes (inodes frozen for cross-rank rename). Lock caches (async dirops) auth-pin dirfrags and increment frozen_inode_suppressed so inodes in them cannot finish freezing; freezing a dir/tree invalidates such lock caches.
features.notes: Connects async create/unlink (kclient) with migration and fragmentation.

features.name: 128-bit waiter masks with ordered lock waiters
features.description: Waiters live in a per-object multimap keyed by sequence; mask bits 0-63 are object-specific (CDir 0-3, CInode 0-4) plus generic WAIT_UNFREEZE(59), WAIT_SINGLEAUTH(60), WAIT_ORDERED(61); bits 64+ hold 4 wait bits per embedded SimpleLock (shift by lock type). Lock waiters get a global FIFO sequence; plain waiters get seq 0 and run first. PIN_WAITER is held while any waiter exists.
features.notes: count_waiters() counts by sequence key, not mask (bug; only affects an export status field).

features.name: Waiter routing
features.description: CDentry forwards WAIT_UNFREEZE/WAIT_SINGLEAUTH to its dir; CDir forwards WAIT_SINGLEAUTH up to the subtree root dir; CInode forwards WAIT_SINGLEAUTH (unless explicitly ambiguous) and WAIT_UNFREEZE (unless itself frozen/freezing) to its parent dir; WAIT_CREATED requires STATE_CREATING.

features.name: Dentry-name waiters
features.description: CDir::waiting_on_dentry maps (name, snapid) to contexts; used by keyed fetches and remote discover; take_dentry_waiting takes a snapid range; split/merge re-homes them by name hash; PIN_DNWAITER while non-empty.

features.name: Synchronous vs queued waiter completion
features.description: MDSCacheObject::finish_waiting runs contexts synchronously in the caller's stack; CDir::finish_waiting runs them synchronously only for r<0 and otherwise appends to MDSRank::finished_queue, which the mds-rank-progr thread drains under mds_lock completing each with r=0.
features.notes: C_MDS_RetryRequest ignores r; errors must be rediscovered by the retried request.

features.name: MDSContext family and IO completion rules
features.description: MDSContext::complete asserts mds_lock held; MDSIOContextBase::complete acquires mds_lock, drops the context when stopping, respawns on -EBLOCKLISTED/-ETIMEDOUT and is tracked (track=true, the default) in a global list for slow-IO health; MDSLogContextBase advances the journal safe pos; C_IO_Wrapper bounces to the finisher; C_MDSInternalNoop; MDSGather.
features.notes: RADOS completions go Objecter -> C_OnFinisher -> single mds-rank-fin thread -> mds_lock.

features.name: Per-dirfrag version sequence and projected fnode (RCU)
features.description: CDir::pre_dirty hands out ++projected_version; every dirtying change to a dentry or primary inode in the frag and every fnode projection consumes one. project_fnode copies the latest fnode (shared_ptr<const>, shared with journal dirlumps) onto a FIFO (a repeat call by the same mutation returns projected_fnode.back()); MutationImpl::apply pops the FRONT projection, not its own. Journal completions of mutations on the same dir can arrive out of order (commit fc0f61ca6ba, tracker 79136), so CDir::mark_dirty returns early for a stale pv instead of asserting; the applied fnode still converges to the newest projection.
features.notes: Cleaning rule: _committed cleans a dirty item once committed_version >= item version; clean items loaded by fetch may carry versions above committed_version.

features.name: Projected dentry linkage (primary/remote/null)
features.description: linkage_t is primary (owns inode), remote (hard link ino + d_type, optional cached inode in remote_parents) or null. push_projected_linkage appends a projection; pop_projected_linkage applies the front one via CDir::link_*_inode (null projections require a prior unlink_inode). use_projected() exposes projected linkage to the xlocking mutation or when the dentry lock allows can_read_projected.
features.notes: Hard links (remote dentries) and atomic visibility of namespace changes.

features.name: Dirty tracking through LogSegment lists
features.description: Dirty dirfrags/dentries/inodes link intrusive items onto the current LogSegment lists; re-dirtying moves them to the newest segment (journal entries carry full state). Never-committed dirfrags stay on the oldest segment's new_dirfrags. try_to_expire commits every dir referenced by the segment's lists (or waits WAIT_UNFREEZE), nudges scatterlocks, stores backtraces, waits for tables, 2PC and purges.

features.name: Write-back driven only by journal segment expiry
features.description: There is no dirty-count or age threshold per dirfrag. Dirfrags are committed when MDLog::trim (mds-log-trim thread) expires their segment (segments > mds_log_max_segments=128 or events > mds_log_max_events=-1, throttled by mds_log_trim_threshold), on 'flush journal' and other MDLog::trim_all callers (rank shutdown in MDCache::shutdown_pass, ScrubStack after repairs), on 'flush_path' (only the dirfrag holding the target inode's dentry, if the inode is dirty), for never-committed source dirfrags and resulting fragments in fragmentation, and for system dirs at mkfs. Nothing is written back once the FS is read-only.
features.notes: Durability for clients comes from the journal, not from dirfrag commits.

features.name: Dirfrag commit (chunked omap writes, header last)
features.description: commit() registers a waiter (first waiter auth-pins the dir); _commit allows one in-flight commit per dirfrag; _omap_commit snapshots dirty dentries under mds_lock; _omap_commit_ops (finisher thread, no mds_lock) emits ops of at most max_dir_commit_size bytes, each guarded by stat for existing objects, with the fnode header set in the last op; _committed cleans dentries/inodes with version <= committed_version, re-commits for later waiters and drops the auth pin.
features.notes: mds_dir_max_commit_size=10 MiB (0 means 0.9*osd_max_write_size = 81 MiB by default); the limit is approximate: entries are never split across ops, so an op carrying an oversized entry exceeds it.

features.name: Commit error handling
features.description: -ENOENT on a never-committed dirfrag under a stray dir counts as success (STATE_MISSINGOBJS on snapshotted dirs). Other errors log to the cluster log and call handle_write_error (mds_action_on_write_error: 0 ignore, 1 read-only (default), 2 respawn; EBLOCKLISTED respawns), leaving commit state and waiters in place.
features.notes: Read-only rank surfaces as MDS_READ_ONLY health; once read-only, MDLog::trim/_maybe_expired return immediately so no further dirfrag commits happen (src/mds/MDLog.cc:727, 935).

features.name: Dirfrag fetch: full, keyed, batched, background prefetch
features.description: fetch() reads header + all omap entries in batches of mds_dir_keys_per_op (16384), single full fetch in flight (STATE_FETCHING) with WAIT_COMPLETE waiters; fetch_keys() reads only named keys and wakes per-name waiters (used directly by rejoin prefetch and batched open_ino, and with an empty key list to load just the header of a version-0 dir); with mds_dir_prefetch=false named fetches become keyed and optional background full prefetches start after mds_dir_prefetch_backend_hit_threshold hits; batched reads restart if a newer commit completes; unlinked dirs under strays are marked complete without IO.
features.notes: Keyed misses create clean null dentries (negative cache).

features.name: Underwater item reconciliation after replay
features.description: When a dirfrag never committed in this cache life is fetched, dirty cached dentries/inodes that exactly match the on-disk copy (same remote target, or same ino and inode version) are marked clean because they were flushed before the previous MDS died.

features.name: Damage detection on fetch
features.description: Missing object, undecodable or oversized fnode header -> go_bad (DamageTable dirfrag damage, STATE_BADFRAG, complete, WAIT_COMPLETE gets -EIO); invalid dentry marker or decode error -> go_bad_dentry (dentry damage, fetch continues); duplicate primary inode -> cluster log 'loaded dup inode'; fatal damage marks the rank damaged.
features.notes: Clients see EIO for damaged entries. Any OSD read error other than ENOENT/ENODATA (and EBLOCKLISTED/ETIMEDOUT, which respawn) trips ceph_assert in _omap_fetched (src/mds/CDir.cc:2063). go_bad does not wake waiting_on_dentry waiters of keyed fetches and does not undo background-fetch accounting (observed in code, runtime effect unverified).

features.name: Directory backtrace verification on fetch
features.description: With mds_verify_backtrace>0 (default 1) the fetch of frag * also reads the 'parent' xattr and verifies the first ancestor; mismatch logs 'bad backtrace on directory inode', re-dirties the backtrace, asserts if >1.
features.notes: Backtraces are what cephfs-data-scan and open-by-ino rely on.

features.name: Snapshot ranges on dentries and snap-aware lookup
features.description: Dentries are valid for [first,last]; head dentries have last=CEPH_NOSNAP; the map key is (hash24, name, last) so several snapshot generations of a name coexist; lookup(name, snap) takes the smallest last >= snap and checks first <= snap.
features.notes: Snapshots are a CephFS extension.

features.name: Stale snapshot dentry purge
features.description: If the realm destroyed snapshots past fnode.snap_purged_thru, fetch skips snapshot dentries that no longer cover any snapshot (keys queued in stale_items, dir re-dirtied without a journal entry) and commit removes such dentries and their keys (try_trim_snap_dentry).
features.notes: Mutates fnode->snap_purged_thru in place via const_cast.

features.name: Dentry 'first' corruption checks
features.description: check_corruption flags first > last or first > snapclient last_seq+1; on load sets corrupt_first_loaded, on commit logs and (mds_abort_on_newly_corrupt_dentry, default true) aborts the MDS; mds_go_bad_corrupt_dentry (default true) records dentry damage. scrub() applies the same checks.
features.notes: check_corruption(true) runs on every CDir::add_*_dentry (fetch, replay, creates); check_corruption(false) from _omap_commit.

features.name: Directory completeness and authoritative negative lookups
features.description: STATE_COMPLETE means every dentry of the dirfrag is cached; a miss is then authoritative ENOENT (path_traverse, open_ino, discover). Set by full fetch, mkdir, system dirs at mkfs/populate_mydir, fragment creation, replay of complete dirlumps, go_bad(complete), stray shortcut; cleared when trimming a non-clean-null auth dentry, trim_non_auth, rejoin of non-auth dirs (MDCache::recalc_auth_bits), replay of importing lumps. Readdir requires completeness.
features.notes: Directory emptiness (rmdir) uses projected fragstat, not completeness.

features.name: Bloom filter of trimmed names
features.description: When a head dentry that is not a clean null is trimmed from an auth dir, its name is added to a per-dir bloom filter before completeness is cleared; the filter is created lazily only when a complete dir is first trimmed (never in standby-replay) and then keeps receiving later trims. A later miss on a name not in the filter is answered ENOENT without fetching. Reset by mark_complete, removed on export and abort_import.
features.notes: Optimization; correctness only requires that every trimmed name is inserted.

features.name: Null dentries and silent drop of NEW dentries
features.description: Null dentries cache non-existence or represent pending deletions (dirty null -> omap_rm_keys at commit). Clean null dentries are trimmable without affecting completeness; readdir removes unreferenced ones. A NEW dentry (never committed) that becomes null is removed with no RADOS deletion (try_remove_unlinked_dn).
features.notes: STATE_NEW is only set on new stray dentries (Server::prepare_stray_dentry); try_remove_unlinked_dn callers are Server::_link_remote_finish, _unlink_local_finish and _rename_apply.

features.name: Dentry LRUs (lru and bottom_lru)
features.description: Only dentries are LRU objects. Auth and remote dentries go to MDCache::lru (midpoint mds_cache_mid=0.7); replica null dentries and replica primary dentries in stray dirs go to bottom_lru (trimmed first). Placement is re-evaluated on link/unlink/auth change; referenced dentries are lru-pinned (pintail). touch_dentry promotes auth dentries to the top.
features.notes: perf mds.inodes* report lru sizes (dentries).

features.name: Dirfrag counters and ENOSPC limit
features.description: CDir keeps head/snap item/null counters (asserted to sum to items.size()), num_dirty and num_inodes_with_caps (open file table hook). get_frag_size() (projected fragstat nfiles+nsubdirs) >= mds_bal_fragment_size_max (100000) makes creates fail with ENOSPC; also drives should_split/should_merge.
features.notes: ENOSPC on a full directory fragment is client-visible.

features.name: Split/merge data movement
features.description: CDir::split creates child CDir objects (replica map, popularity scaled by 1/2^bits, dir_auth, freeze_tree_state, FRAGMENT_KEPT|COMPLETE bits); merge runs on an already constructed CDir (dir_auth/freeze_tree_state from the first sub, max nonce per replica, union of kept bits). Both move each dentry with steal_dentry (re-accounting fragstat/rstat, dirty lists, nested auth pins), re-home dentry waiters, set the new fnode version (split: old version; merge: highest sub version) and hand outstanding unaccounted deltas to the first/merged fragment; new auth fragments start frozen-dir and complete.

features.name: frag_t/fragtree_t and name-hash frag selection
features.description: frag_t = 8-bit bit count + 24-bit value using the most significant bits; a hash belongs to a frag if (h & mask) == value (low 24 bits of the 32-bit hash). fragtree_t stores split points only; operator[] maps a hash to its leaf; pick_dirfrag hashes with the dir layout's dl_dir_hash (default rjenkins).
features.notes: Shared with clients for request routing and readdir positions. For legacy dl_dir_hash 0/LINUX layouts the kclient routes with the kernel dcache d_name.hash, which differs from ceph_str_hash_linux.

features.name: DirStat (frag, auth, dist) in client replies
features.description: encode_dirstat sends frag, dir_auth.first (-1 = same as inode auth) and the replica set (only when the dir is auth, replicated and requests are not forced to auth), versioned when the session has CEPHFS_FEATURE_REPLY_ENCODING. kclient uses it to route reads to replicas and to the frag's auth; libcephfs updates fragmap/frag_repmap.

features.name: Readdir order follows dentry key order
features.description: CDir::items is ordered by (24-bit hash value, name, snapid); readdir walks it from lower_bound(offset key) and, if the client asks for reply bitflags, sets CEPH_READDIR_HASH_ORDER|CEPH_READDIR_OFFSET_HASH so clients encode f_pos from the hash and resume by offset_hash.
features.notes: Stable resumable readdir (telldir/seekdir semantics) depends on it.

features.name: Cache memory accounting
features.description: CDentry, CDir, scrub_info_t and ClientLease and most of their containers are allocated in mempool mds_co; cache_size() = mds_co bytes vs mds_cache_memory_limit (4 GiB) with reservation 0.05 drives trimming; > 1.5x raises MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED. Counter<CDentry>/Counter<CDir> feed mds_mem dn/dir perf counters.
features.notes: Bloom filters, lock side allocations, freeze_tree_state, batch_ops are not in the pool.

features.name: Client dentry leases anchored on CDentry
features.description: ClientLease records (dentry, session, seq from ++session->lease_seq, ttl) live in CDentry::client_leases; the first lease sets the dentry lock LEASED flag and PIN_CLIENTLEASE; removing the last kicks eval_gather if the lock was transitioning.
features.notes: Lease protocol itself is documented on the leases page.

features.name: Dentry versionlock pipelining
features.description: When a request xlocks a dentry on its authority, acquire_locks adds a wrlock on CEPH_LOCK_DVERSION for leaders (pipelined journal updates) or an xlock for peers (no other journal updates, safe rollback).

features.name: CDir/CDentry migration encodings
features.description: encode_export/decode_import ship fnode, dirty_old_rstat, committed_version, state, dir_rep, popularity and replicas (dir) or first/state/versions/lock/replicas (dentry), with state masks deciding what survives. After export the old authority becomes a replica with EXPORT_NONCE (Migrator::finish_export_dir for dirs, CDentry::finish_export for dentries); CDir::abort_import also reverts to replica with EXPORT_NONCE.
features.notes: MDS-to-MDS only.

features.name: Admin dumps of dirfrags and dentries
features.description: dump dir <path> [dentry_dump], get subtrees, dump tree, dump cache, dump inode emit CDir/CDentry/MDSCacheObject JSON (versions, dir_auth, states, replicas, nonce, auth_pins, freeze flags, pins, dentry linkage); CDentry::dump emits auth_pins twice.
features.notes: Used heavily by QA tooling.

features.name: Health signals from this layer
features.description: MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO (IO contexts older than osd_op_complaint_time=30s), MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED, MDS_TRIM when slow commits block segment expiry, MDS_DAMAGE and rank damaged from go_bad, MDS_READ_ONLY after commit errors.

features.name: Lookup/getattr batching on dentries
features.description: CDentry::batch_ops (keyed by mask) lets identical concurrent lookups share one execution; the destructor asserts no batch op remains.

features.name: Open-file-table tracking of dirfrags with capped inodes
features.description: num_inodes_with_caps counts primary inodes with caps in the dirfrag; transitions 0<->1 add/remove the dirfrag from the open file table so recovery can prefetch it.
features.notes: See RADOS catalog / mds tables pages for the open file table.

features.name: Dirfrag popularity and replication hint
features.description: CDir keeps decaying popularity vectors (pop_me, pop_nested, pop_auth_subtree, pop_auth_subtree_nested; mds_decay_halflife=5s); on hot reads the balancer sets dir_rep=REP_ALL above mds_bal_replicate_threshold (8000) and broadcasts MDirUpdate to active ranks that are not yet replicas, which then discover (replicate) the dirfrag; the resulting replica_map entries are what get_dist_spec advertises to clients in DirStat.dist.

features.name: Read-only mode stops dirfrag write-back
features.description: After a write error forces read-only (mds_action_on_write_error=1), MDLog::trim and MDLog::_maybe_expired return immediately, log_mark_dirty is skipped and flush_path returns EROFS, so dirty dirfrags are never committed again in this rank life; the failed commit's STATE_COMMITTING, waiters and auth pin stay in place.
features.notes: Visible as MDS_READ_ONLY.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock protects all CDir/CDentry/MDSCacheObject state
serialization_points.shared_state: Dentry maps, counters, versions, projections, pins, auth pins, waiters, freeze state, LRU links, LogSegment lists
serialization_points.why_serialized: No per-object locks exist; the single coarse lock is the concurrency model
serialization_points.notes: Operations on unrelated dirfrags/dentries share no state.

serialization_points.name: Per-dirfrag version sequence
serialization_points.why_serialized: Every dirtying change to any dentry or primary inode in the frag (and every fnode projection) takes the next version; cleanliness is committed_version >= item version
serialization_points.notes: Only monotonicity per dirfrag and comparison with committed_version are relied upon.

serialization_points.name: Projected fnode FIFO
serialization_points.shared_state: CDir::projected_fnode, CDir::fnode (fragstat, rstat, mtime, change_attr, version)
serialization_points.why_serialized: Each mutation copies the latest projected fnode and appends it; apply pops the front, so apply order must equal projection order
serialization_points.notes: Count/rstat changes are additive, mtime is max, change_attr increments; only the frag's journal order matters.

serialization_points.name: Dentry projected linkage
serialization_points.why_serialized: Protected by the dentry xlock; FIFO application
serialization_points.notes: Two operations on the same name genuinely conflict.

serialization_points.name: Dentry versionlock
serialization_points.why_serialized: Leaders wrlock to pipeline journal updates; peers xlock so that no other journal update interleaves with a rollback-able peer update

serialization_points.name: Single in-flight commit per dirfrag
serialization_points.why_serialized: A newer commit waits until the in-flight one completes
serialization_points.notes: Successive commits of one object must be applied in version order; nothing else conflicts.

serialization_points.name: Single in-flight full fetch per dirfrag
Whole-dirfrag processing inside one mds_lock critical section
serialization_points.shared_state: All items of one dirfrag (up to 100000+ entries)
serialization_points.why_serialized: Decode/encode and clean-marking loops run under the global lock with periodic heartbeat resets
serialization_points.notes: Blocks the whole rank for the duration.

serialization_points.name: Tree freeze for migration
serialization_points.shared_state: freeze_tree_state (shared counter), auth pins of all dirfrags in the subtree
serialization_points.why_serialized: Authority change requires no in-flight mutation in the subtree; new auth pins are refused while freezing
serialization_points.notes: Quiescing the moved subtree is inherent to moving authority; the subtree walk and single shared counter are implementation choices.

serialization_points.name: Dir freeze for fragmentation
serialization_points.shared_state: auth pins of the dirfrag and its direct dentries/inodes
serialization_points.why_serialized: split/merge move CDentry objects between CDir containers

serialization_points.name: Nested auth-pin accounting
serialization_points.why_serialized: Every auth pin on a dentry or primary inode updates its dirfrag's counter (and the subtree counter while freezing)
serialization_points.notes: Counters are only consulted by freeze logic.

serialization_points.name: Global dentry LRUs
serialization_points.shared_state: Intrusive LRU lists (top/bottom/pintail) for all dentries of the rank
serialization_points.why_serialized: Every dentry add/remove/touch/pin/unpin edits shared lists

serialization_points.name: Current LogSegment dirty lists
serialization_points.shared_state: dirty_dirfrags, new_dirfrags, dirty_dentries, dirty_inodes of the current segment
serialization_points.why_serialized: Every dirty mark relinks the object onto the newest segment of the single rank journal
serialization_points.notes: Tied to the single journal stream per rank.

serialization_points.name: Process-wide statics
serialization_points.shared_state: Freeze fast-path counters, global waiter sequence

serialization_points.name: Waiter queue drained by one progress thread
serialization_points.why_serialized: All queued waiters (fetch done, commit done, unfreeze, single auth) are completed one by one under mds_lock

serialization_points.name: Single finisher thread for IO completions
serialization_points.why_serialized: One Finisher thread, then mds_lock again
serialization_points.notes: Also runs C_IO_Dir_Commit_Ops (a plain Context) without mds_lock; it reads the live CDir::fnode shared_ptr while mds_lock holders may reset it.

serialization_points.name: Lock-cache auth pins on dirfrags
serialization_points.why_serialized: Async dirop lock caches hold long-lived auth pins that block freezes until invalidated

serialization_points.name: Segment expiry on the mds-log-trim thread
serialization_points.shared_state: Journal segments, their dirty lists, and every dirty dirfrag they reference
serialization_points.why_serialized: One upkeep thread periodically calls MDLog::trim under mds_lock; expiry commits all dirfrags of the expiring segments in one pass, throttled only by mds_log_trim_threshold
serialization_points.notes: Write-back timing for every dirfrag is coupled to the single journal's segment boundaries.

external_contract.detail: frag (u32), auth (s32, -1 = same as dir inode auth), dist (set<s32> -> ndist + entries); wrapped in ENCODE_START(1,1) when the session has CEPHFS_FEATURE_REPLY_ENCODING (kclient parses struct_v>=1, compat==1). dist is empty unless the dirfrag is auth, replicated and mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth=false.

kclient stores frag.mds and up to 4 dist ranks; USE_ANY_MDS requests may go to a random replica in dist, otherwise to frag.mds, otherwise to the auth cap. The MDS must accept or forward requests arriving at any advertised rank.
auth >= 0 sets fragmap[frag]=auth, negative erases it; frag forced to leaf in the client fragtree; dist accepted only from the auth rank's replies.

external_contract.item: Dentry name hash and frag selection
external_contract.detail: MDS computes ceph_str_hash(dl_dir_hash, name) (0 means CEPH_STR_HASH_LINUX = ceph_str_hash_linux) and selects frags from the low 24 bits with the shared frag_t encoding (8-bit bits | 24-bit value). New dirs use mds_default_dir_hash=2 (rjenkins), for which the kclient computes the same hash; for legacy 0/LINUX layouts the kclient routes with the kernel dcache d_name.hash (not ceph_str_hash_linux), so routing is only a hint and the MDS forwards.

external_contract.item: Readdir hash ordering and offset_hash resume
external_contract.detail: Entries are returned in dentry_key_t order (24-bit hash, name, snapid). When the request asks for reply bitflags the MDS sets CEPH_READDIR_HASH_ORDER|CEPH_READDIR_OFFSET_HASH; the kclient recomputes raw_hash = ceph_str_hash(dl_dir_hash, name) per entry, builds f_pos from ceph_frag_value(raw_hash) and resumes using offset_hash/offset_str (lower_bound on the dentry map).
libcephfs/ceph-fuse/Ganesha readdir resumption relies on the same hash-ordered dentry listing and offset_hash semantics.
Negative lookups are answered from complete dirfrags, null dentries or the bloom filter of trimmed names; must never be wrong.
Creates/links/renames into a dirfrag whose projected fragstat size >= mds_bal_fragment_size_max (100000) fail with ENOSPC.

external_contract.item: EIO for damaged metadata; hidden readdir entries
external_contract.detail: Damaged dirfrags/dentries (missing object, corrupt fnode, invalid dentry value) produce EIO via DamageTable; readdir skips STATE_BADREMOTEINO remote dentries, purging strays and the CEPH_INO_CEPH inode.

MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO (MDSIOContextBase older than osd_op_complaint_time), MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED (mds_co bytes > 1.5 x mds_cache_memory_limit), MDS_TRIM (segments > 2 x mds_log_max_segments), MDS_DAMAGE, MDS_READ_ONLY after commit errors; fatal damage marks the rank damaged.

external_contract.item: Perf counters used by ceph fs status and the dashboard
external_contract.detail: mgr/status reads mds_mem.dn, mds_mem.ino, mds_mem.dir, mds_mem.cap; dashboard reads mds.inodes, mds.caps, mds_mem.ino among others. mds.inodes is the dentry LRU size.

Object '<ino hex>.<frag %08x>' in the metadata pool; reads: omap_get_header + omap_get_vals (16384 per op) or omap_get_vals_by_keys + getxattr parent (FAILOK); writes: optional stat guard, omap_rm_keys, omap_set, header in the last op, size-limited by mds_dir_max_commit_size.

external_contract.item: Offline tools depend on the C++ dirfrag format
external_contract.detail: cephfs-data-scan, first-damage.py, cephfs-meta-injection and cephfs-journal-tool read/write dirfrag omap keys ('name_head', 'name_<snapid hex>') and values directly.
dump dir, get subtrees, dump tree, dump cache, dump inode expose CDir/CDentry/MDSCacheObject fields (versions, dir_auth, states, replicas, auth_pins, pins).

rust_implications.topic: Dirfrag as the natural unit of concurrency
rust_implications.implication: Almost all mutable state on this page (dentry map, counters, version sequence, fnode projections, dirty list, commit/fetch state, completeness, bloom) is per dirfrag. A Rust shard can own whole dirfrags with their own lock/actor; cross-dirfrag interactions are limited to parent-inode stats (fragstat/rstat scatter), rename and subtree/fragment restructuring.

rust_implications.topic: Replace the projected-fnode FIFO with delta accumulation
rust_implications.implication: C++ copies the whole fnode per mutation and relies on FIFO apply order. Creates/unlinks in one directory only need additive deltas (nfiles/nsubdirs/rstat), max(mtime) and an increment of change_attr; journaling deltas per shard allows concurrent creates in the same dirfrag to proceed without a full-copy FIFO, which matters for the NFS/Ganesha many-creates-per-directory use case.

The only properties consumed are per-dirfrag monotonic versions and committed_version >= item version for cleanliness; an atomic per-dirfrag counter (or the shard journal sequence) suffices. Journal replay must be able to reconstruct which items are clean after a crash (C++ uses 'underwater' matching when committed_version==0).

C++ commits dirfrags only when a journal segment expires. With per-shard journals, write-back should be per shard and driven by that shard's journal trim, so one hot subvolume cannot force commits (or MDS_TRIM warnings) for others.

The on-disk format is free, but the invariant 'header (version marker) written after all entries, ops ordered per object' must be kept or replaced (e.g. single atomic op when small, version-tagged entries otherwise). Avoid the C++ race of encoding the live fnode outside the lock: snapshot the header together with the entries.

rust_implications.topic: Large dirfrags off the critical path
rust_implications.implication: C++ decodes/encodes whole dirfrags (up to 100k+ entries) under the global lock with heartbeat resets. Decode/encode should run off the shard's critical section and publish results atomically.

rust_implications.topic: Auth pins and freezing as shard quiescence
rust_implications.implication: Freeze semantics (refuse new pins, drain in-flight, never block while holding pins, retry whole operation) are what migration and fragmentation need. In a sharded design this maps to a per-shard in-flight counter and an admission gate; the subtree walk with a shared counter is not required if shards have stable identity.

Replace per-object 128-bit waiter multimaps with async wait queues per object/lock. Keep FIFO ordering for lock waiters, avoid synchronous completion in the caller's stack (C++ mixes both), and propagate error codes explicitly instead of retry-and-rediscover.

The 'ancestors are pinned' invariant makes eviction leaf-first and keeps paths resolvable. A Rust cache should either keep this invariant per shard or make objects addressable by id without requiring cached ancestors; LRUs should be per shard to avoid a global list touched on every lookup.

POSIX ENOENT correctness requires an explicit notion of 'complete' per dirfrag (or authoritative negative entries). The bloom filter is optional; if used, every trimmed name of a complete dirfrag must be inserted before completeness is dropped.

Keep: dentry hash = ceph_str_hash(dl_dir_hash, name) with rjenkins default; frag_t 8+24-bit encoding and 24-bit hash selection; readdir order by (24-bit hash, name, snapid) with HASH_ORDER/OFFSET_HASH flags; DirStat (frag, auth with -1 meaning inode auth, dist) and its versioned envelope; ENOSPC at mds_bal_fragment_size_max.

If the Rust MDS never advertises replicas (empty dist, auth -1 or explicit), kclient routes all requests to the auth rank, which keeps the protocol valid and avoids implementing read replicas initially.

If snapshots are supported, dentries must carry [first,last] ranges and lookups must be snapid-aware; stale snapshot entries must be purged lazily. A minimal POSIX MDS can defer snapshot support but must still reject/handle snapdir requests consistently.
To keep 'ceph fs status' and the dashboard functional, emit mds_mem.dn/ino/dir/cap and mds.inodes/caps with the same names, even if their meaning is approximated per shard and summed.
Emit MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO (age of in-flight metadata IO), MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED and MDS_TRIM equivalents, aggregated over shards, since mon/mgr and operators rely on them.

Because the RADOS format is free, cephfs-data-scan, first-damage.py, cephfs-meta-injection and cephfs-journal-tool will not work; the Rust project needs its own recovery/inspection tooling or must document their absence.

C++ installs projected fnodes FIFO regardless of which mutation completes, and journal completions can arrive out of order. A Rust design should either apply per-dirfrag deltas commutatively or carry an explicit per-dirfrag sequence so that out-of-order completion cannot expose a later mutation's state early.

Treat any dirfrag read error as damage or retry rather than a process abort, and make sure every waiter class (complete, per-name, background slot) is released on every failure path; the C++ go_bad path misses per-name waiters and background-fetch accounting.

open_questions: CDir::_omap_commit_ops runs without mds_lock and encodes the live *fnode into the header (src/mds/CDir.cc:2516) while the batch was snapshotted earlier: can the header describe a newer fnode version than the dentries written in that commit, and does replay/fetch ever depend on header-version consistency? (unverified)

MutationImpl::apply pops the front projected fnode/inode rather than its own, and journal completions of mutations on the same dir do arrive out of order (commit fc0f61ca6ba, tracker 79136, made CDir::mark_dirty tolerate a stale pv). Which paths complete out of order, and can a commit taken while the applied fnode contains a not-yet-applied mutation's projection persist state whose journal entry is not yet safe? (unverified)
_omap_fetched mutates fnode->snap_purged_thru in place through const_cast on a shared_ptr<const fnode_t> that may also be referenced by an in-flight journal event; is this observable? (unverified)
count_waiters(mask) counts multimap entries by sequence key; is unfreeze_tree_waiters in export status relied upon by any tooling? (appears always 0)
On a non-ENOENT commit error, _committed returns without clearing STATE_COMMITTING or waiters; after the rank goes read-only, are these waiters ever released before respawn? (unverified)

Migrator::dispatch_export_dir adds a WAIT_CREATED waiter when the dir inode has no applied parent dentry; CDir::add_waiter asserts STATE_CREATING. Code reading suggests this only happens for a mkdir'ed dir before its journal entry applies (mark_new clears STATE_CREATING at the same time) and system dirs are excluded from export, so it looks safe; not verified at runtime.

go_bad on a keyed fetch (mds_dir_prefetch=false, rejoin prefetch, batched open_ino) does not take waiting_on_dentry waiters; do such requests hang when a dirfrag object is missing or its header is corrupt? (unverified)

A background full fetch that hits go_bad never clears STATE_BACKEND_FETCH or decrements MDCache::num_backend_fetching; with mds_dir_prefetch_backend_max=1 background prefetch would stop for the rank's life. (unverified at runtime)
_omap_fetched asserts r in {0, -ENOENT, -ENODATA}: does any OSD error path (EIO on a bad omap read) reach it and crash the rank in practice? (unverified)
go_bad(true) on a fresh dir sets fnode version 1 without updating projected_version (0), so the next pre_dirty reuses version 1; can a BADFRAG dir still be mutated and committed? (unverified)
